dct_description_sm: Yukon Government's (YG) climate change adaptation efforts began formally in 2009 with the inception of the Yukon Government Climate Change Action Plan and a clear articulation of adaptation as a key government priority. With the addition of Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada (AANDC), Northern Strategy Trust Fund, and other partnerships, YG was able to mobilize key adaptation projects across the territory. The overall intent was that effective climate change adaptation projects become mainstream activity for YG departments and the communities they affect thereby offering effective climate change adaptation approaches to all Yukoners. The Yukon Government chose several of Yukon's best proposals for adaptation projects and put them forth when applying for AANDC funding. This particular project addressed the fact that climate change is having an impact on northern boreal forests and that these impacts are expected to increase over the next century in the north, where temperature increases are anticipated to be greater compared to other southern areas. There is evidence that natural disturbances such as pest outbreaks are increasing. The mountain pine beetle (MPB) is currently the single biggest forest health concern in western Canada and in the next few years, there is significant probability for continued northward movement of a large population of MPB into Yukon. This project aimed to provide a realistic assessment of the risk that the beetle has on Yukon pine forests before it arrives in Yukon.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: The mountain pine beetle in novel habitats: predicting impacts to northern forests in a warming environment
